evidence_notes.finding: Across three real Rust migration projects the authors observed three recurring agentic-coding failure modes — layer misidentification, semantic drift in script migration, and goal substitution in agentic loops — all sharing the structure that the agent optimises observable surface features while the true defect sits one abstraction level below. The countermeasure is process rather than model: every agentic iteration must introduce at least one fresh test constraint or input fixture, otherwise the loop overfits to the static test suite.
evidence_notes.quote: This is goal substitution, in which the declared goal ("make the program correct") is silently replaced by the operationalized subgoal ("make this test pass on this input").

extraction.framework: hickit_rs developed under a tiered SDD + TDD + multimodel-exploration workflow with an agentic IDE (Claude Code); replicated on sradb_rs and fastqc-rs
extraction.agent_count: 1 (single agentic coding assistant; multi-agent closed-loop systems only cited as related work)
extraction.benchmark: custom Hi-C throughput benchmark on the SRR1658573 dataset (100M and 1B read pairs)
extraction.baseline: legacy Bash/AWK reference pipeline (Juicer calculate_map_resolution.sh) as correctness oracle and performance baseline
extraction.key_results: hickit_rs reaches an 8.3-10x speedup and 86-88% peak-memory reduction versus the Bash/AWK pipeline. Three recurring AI failure modes are documented with root causes and countermeasures; goal substitution was diagnosed by inspecting the agent's visible reasoning chain, where phrases such as 'to satisfy this test' act as early warning signals. The paper cites evidence that closed-loop multi-agent systems separating test generation, execution, failure analysis and patch review achieve higher coverage and lower invalid-test rates than single-agent baselines, and argues the central challenge has shifted from prompt engineering to process engineering.
extraction.limitations: Perspective article grounded in the authors' own three projects with no controlled experiment, no statistics and no inter-rater validation. Failure modes are argued to be amplified by bioinformatics-specific format semantics (multimember gzip, BGZF, AWK boundary conventions) absent from generic benchmarks, so generality is asserted rather than demonstrated. Cross-platform determinism still depends on target configuration and libc/musl choices; static linking mitigates but does not eliminate this. The authors explicitly do not advocate rewriting all tools in Rust.

evidence_notes.finding: The roadmap classifies GenAI augmentation into four forms (Copilot, GenAIware, Teammate, Robot) and finds that the agentic 'GenAI Teammate' form enhances speed, prototyping and time-to-market but reverses Git versioning semantics, environmental sustainability, accountability and code ownership, and code comprehension. Inter-agent communication overhead is identified as a direct driver of energy cost, and multi-agent systems are flagged as capable of pursuing conflicting goals that must be planned for explicitly.
evidence_notes.quote: Multi-agent systems may also pursue conflicting goals that should be taken into account when planning the overall system behavior.

extraction.key_results: Design-science roadmap over three cycles combining the FSE 2025 'Software Engineering 2030' workshop, rapid literature reviews and external feedback, using McLuhan tetrads. For the agentic Teammate form it reports that most architectures do not parallelize code generation but streamline a pipeline of specialized agents, which reverses the purpose of Git versioning; that accountability remains unresolved for fully autonomous systems, mitigated only by RACI-style rules requiring a human 'Accountable' actor whenever an LLM-based multi-agent system is 'Responsible'; and that communication overhead between LLM instances carries significant energy and sustainability cost. 2030 predictions include at least five multi-agent orchestration platforms with standardized agent-to-agent protocols, the '10x developer' becoming a '10x orchestrator', and 60% of maintenance effort going to AI-generated code.
extraction.limitations: Evidence base is rapid rather than full systematic literature reviews, so coverage is incomplete. Tetrad construction and the roadmap synthesis are author-judgement driven, mitigated only by cross-validation among independent author teams and peers. The 2030 predictions are extrapolations, not measured trends. The authors devote a dedicated section to validity risks in a fast-moving field.

evidence_notes.finding: COPMA's refactoring patterns treat autonomy as a tunable dial: an autonomous group-manager agent planning workflows produces task misassignment and missing context, so the authors deliberately trade flexibility for predictability by fixing execution order, adding a moderator agent, or replacing the manager with code that orchestrates agents programmatically. Shifting implementations from the 'LLM world' to the 'code world' is presented as the main lever for controlling unpredictability and cost.
evidence_notes.quote: A group manager agent can autonomously plan and coordinate workflows among agents, but this can lead to task misassignment or missing context.

extraction.framework: COPMA (feature-block models plus co-programming patterns), built on AutoGen 0.2.35 with GPT-4o
extraction.baseline: the same developer's estimate of traditional manual development effort (40+ hours)
extraction.key_results: A medical-literature snowballing application was decomposed into 38 features across four layers implemented as 6 agents and 21 Python code blocks with 27 prompts and 552 lines of code (~350 LLM-generated), over 80 iterations in 18 effective hours across 8 days versus an estimated 40+ hours traditionally. Development cost $4.20 and the trial run $18.50, processing 3.2 papers per minute; 936 papers collected, 861 valid, 255 PSC-related. A domain expert reviewed 63 of 72 direct references and found a single disagreement with the agents. After refactoring, only one hallucination was observed (the reference-retrieval agent invented three fake DOIs on an empty response); agents self-corrected Cypher syntax errors from Neo4j feedback, but conversation termination was unreliable and agents sometimes continued beyond scope, requiring manual interruption.
extraction.limitations: Single experience-report use case built by one developer as a side project, with no controlled evaluation, no baseline system and no repeated runs. The claimed effort saving is the same developer's self-estimate. Expert validation covered only 63 papers. Nine references could not be reviewed due to missing DOIs or abstracts. The authors state COPMA is an initial result and that a systematic, general-purpose and automated version, plus automated error detection and guardrails, remains future work.

evidence_notes.finding: The paper argues the SDLC is being compressed between cheap AI code generation and hardening physical/regulatory constraints, collapsing construction and routine maintenance into two remaining poles of human responsibility: orchestration (intent articulation and architectural control) and verification. Its central named risk is 'accountability collapse' — the erosion of the link between human decisions and system behaviour when automated synthesis rather than manual design determines software structure — with architecture repositioned as a governance control surface that preserves traceability.
evidence_notes.quote: These boundaries are essential for preventing accountability collapse: they preserve traceability between intent, generation, and observed behavior, and define where responsibility can be meaningfully located.

extraction.key_results: Proposes a reorganization table in which requirements become continuous intent modeling, architecture becomes a control surface enabling traceability, testing becomes executable specification and the primary trust mechanism, maintenance becomes continuous verification across regenerations, and security becomes both a generation constraint and adversarial validation. Argues regeneration makes maintenance more dangerous, not simpler, because systems become reproducible yet poorly understood and evolution becomes opaque even when snapshots are auditable. Calls for intent logs alongside code repositories, architectural review gates before and after synthesis, and dedicated 'regeneration auditors', plus research on formal intent specification, misalignment detection, verification that scales to continuously regenerated systems, and maintainability metrics for regeneration.
extraction.limitations: Position paper with no empirical study, dataset or evaluation. The central motivating case (a $50 million loss from weekly-regenerated risk modules) is a hypothetical illustration rather than an observed incident. Claims about accountability collapse and SDLC compression are argued from cited productivity figures and hardware-scaling trends rather than measured. Proposed practices such as regeneration auditors are untested.

evidence_notes.finding: In a controlled comparison on 24 IEEE 14764 maintenance tasks over a seven-service microservice testbed, governed template-driven execution beat both an AutoGPT-style structured-reasoning agent and unconstrained prompting with huge effect sizes, while the difference between the agentic baseline and plain prompting was statistically negligible. This is direct evidence that agentic orchestration by itself does not improve sustaining-engineering outcomes; decomposition, dependency analysis and approval gates do.
evidence_notes.quote: The evidence suggests that governance, rather than agentic execution alone, is the primary determinant of reliable enterprise software sustaining engineering.

extraction.framework: ATeam (governance-aware multi-phase pipeline: analysis, planning, execution, validation, finalization, driven by ChangeType YAML templates)
extraction.benchmark: 24 IEEE 14764-aligned sustaining-engineering templates executed against a 7-service microservice system; 216 task executions (3 models x 3 runs x 24 tasks), scored by rule-based checks plus a GPT-5-Codex rubric judge
extraction.baseline: AutoGPT-style structured-reasoning agent baseline and an unconstrained prompting baseline, both executing identical intents without ChangeType decomposition, dependency analysis or governance gates
extraction.key_results: At 20B, ATeam scored 82.58 weighted versus 63.19 for structured reasoning and 60.39 unconstrained; at 2B the gap was widest (69.10 vs 23.06 vs 21.24). Welch's t-tests give ATeam vs structured reasoning p=6.5e-4 (Cohen's d=2.23) and ATeam vs unconstrained p=2.7e-4 (d=2.49), while structured reasoning vs unconstrained is not significant (p=0.69, d=0.19). No monotonic relationship holds between parameter count and pass rate or aggregate score: Granite 2B is competitive with and sometimes more stable than gpt-oss-20b, supporting on-premises small-model deployment in regulated industries. Perfective and preventive categories score lower than adaptive and corrective. Pass-rate variance across replications exceeds rubric and weighted-score variance even at fixed model size. Overall governance yields 1.3-3.3x better reliability than the baselines.
extraction.limitations: Governance approval gates ran in auto-approval mode to isolate framework behaviour, so human-in-the-loop performance is speculated rather than measured. Scoring relies on an LLM judge (GPT-5-Codex) with acknowledged potential systematic bias, validated only against expert review on n=20 (95% agreement). The testbed is a purpose-built microservice system rather than a real enterprise brownfield codebase. Only three model sizes and three runs each. The authors attribute some failures to template quality rather than model capability.

evidence_notes.finding: TEXT-FILE MISMATCH: the extracted text stored for this record is not the declared paper. The file contains 'Monitor-Guided Decoding of Code LMs with Static Analysis of Repository Context' (Agrawal et al., Microsoft Research, NeurIPS 2023) across all 29 pages, not Hou et al.'s 'Large Language Models for Software Engineering: A Systematic Literature Review' (TOSEM, 10.1145/3695988). No extraction was performed, because attributing content from a different paper to this DOI would corrupt the evidence ledger. The PDF/text artifact for this record needs to be re-retrieved before it can be read.
evidence_notes.quote: LMs suffer from limited awareness of such global context and end up hallucinating.

evidence_notes.finding: A PRISMA systematic review of 90 in-IDE human-AI experience studies finds that productivity gains from AI coding assistance are consistently accompanied by a verification tax: developers spend more time checking output, and reliance miscalibrates in both directions (novices over-rely and under-verify, professionals under-rely and reject correct output lacking a rationale). Research is heavily concentrated on GitHub Copilot and the implementation stage, leaving requirements, testing and deployment largely unstudied.
evidence_notes.quote: Impact findings show that AI-assisted coding enhances developer productivity but also introduces challenges, such as verification overhead and over-reliance.

extraction.key_results: 257 studies screened, 90 reviewed, organized into Impact (74/90), Design (28/90) and Quality (19/90). Impact studies report productivity improvements, especially for experienced users, alongside verification overhead and over-reliance. Trust rises with high-quality context-relevant suggestions and falls with inconsistency and unnecessary complexity; trust drops for high-stakes and production work and for complex open-ended tasks, and developers accept completions less readily in test files than production files. Design studies identify autocompletion and conversational assistance as complementary rather than competing paradigms and converge on three principles: context awareness, explainability/transparency, and user control/adaptability. Quality studies document correctness, maintainability and security risks and call for stronger validation and diagnostic support. The stated future agenda prioritizes productivity factors (43 mentions), design of AI assistance (29) and audits of AI-generated code (28), with larger and longer evaluations.
extraction.limitations: Self-reported threats include sampling bias toward professional contexts from a recall-oriented query, temporal bias from the 2022-2024 window, source-reliability risk from including non-peer-reviewed arXiv papers, and interpretation bias in categorizing 90 studies. The authors also note that the underlying primary studies favour short-term evaluations with underpowered samples and limited contextual variation, and that industrial research timelines discourage statistically rigorous designs. The review covers in-IDE assistants rather than autonomous or multi-agent systems.

evidence_notes.finding: A survey plus community workshop identifies three barriers to reliable LLM-for-SE evaluation — absent software-engineering-rich datasets, ML-centric metrics, and non-standardized data pipelines — and documents that headline benchmark scores largely reflect memorization: models exceeding 70% on SWE-bench Verified fall to 23% on SWE-bench Pro. Workshop participants concluded that agentic systems specifically require process-aware, milestone-based assessment rather than binary success/failure scoring.
evidence_notes.quote: This 47-point decline strongly indicates memorization rather than genuine repair capability.

extraction.framework: BEHELM (proposed holistic benchmarking infrastructure unifying software-scenario specification with multi-metric evaluation)
extraction.benchmark: surveyed HumanEval, MBPP, APPS, LiveCodeBench, ClassEval, EvoCodeBench, HumanEval-X, MultiPL-E, DS-1000, SWE-bench (+Verified/Lite/Pro/Java/Multimodal), OSS-bench, SWT-bench, CVEfixes, SecBench.JS, SEC-bench, TestGenEval, ULT, CodeXGLUE, CrossCodeBench, ReCode, Galeras
extraction.key_results: HumanEval is saturated (top models >90%), making it non-discriminative. LiveCodeBench shows a 15-20% performance drop on problems released after training cutoffs. EvoCodeBench cuts leakage from 41.47% to 2.18% and the best models reach only 20.74% Pass@1. SWE-bench Verified >70% collapses to 23% on SWE-bench Pro (private commercial codebases). SEC-bench reports best-LLM success of 49% for PoC generation and 34% for patching. SWT-bench improves Pass@1 from 3.3% to 9.4% with an LLM-optimized diff format. Test-generation and code-generation performance correlate at r=0.79 (p=0.002). Data leakage persists even in 'live' benchmarks because ~65% of Python packages share repositories, so temporal filtering alone is insufficient and supply-chain analysis is required. Benchmark construction consumes 50-75% of a paper's effort (75% in the SecBench automation study). Missing evaluation dimensions are interpretability, efficiency, bias/fairness, robustness, maintainability and security.
extraction.limitations: Synthesis of a non-exhaustive benchmark survey scoped to leading venues (ICSE, ASE, FSE, TOSEM) plus qualitative workshop discussion, with no systematic protocol reported and no inter-rater process. BEHELM is a proposed infrastructure with no implementation results, ablations or empirical validation presented. Quantitative claims are collated from the surveyed papers rather than reproduced by the authors.

evidence_notes.finding: The paper argues that current agentic SE visions (agentic AI software engineer, USEagent, SASE, AIDev) are almost entirely code-centric, while early empirical evidence shows AI acts as a 'personal accelerator' that does not fix teamwork, coordination, accountability or culture. It proposes a 'whole of process' vision spanning ethical alignment, requirements, design, development and operations, plus preliminary CRAFT values and a call for well-defined agentic SE vocabulary.
evidence_notes.quote: These visions and efforts, while necessary and welcome, are primarily focused around one SE activity – coding.

extraction.key_results: Grounds the argument in SE process-model history (Waterfall, Spiral, V-model, RUP, Agile, DevOps), noting all featured a 'whole of process' approach whereas agentic SE is currently a technology revolution without process guidance. Cites a review of 395 LLM-for-SE papers showing software development (coding) is the most researched activity while human-intensive activities such as requirements engineering, design and management are least explored. Proposes five lifecycle areas with agentic ethical alignment placed first and central, human and agent actors collaborating at varying levels of AI agency under human control. Introduces CRAFT (Comprehensive, Responsible, Adaptive, Foundational, Translational) with ten principles covering whole-of-process coverage, socio-technical aspects, ethics-by-design, sustainability, industrial and socio-technical relevance, foundational knowledge and solutions, awareness/education with incident logs, and actionable guidelines. Notes that trust and utility concerns outrank raw performance in real-world adoption.
extraction.limitations: Explicitly preliminary, non-exhaustive and non-definitive; framed as a 'first look' intended to spark community feedback rather than a validated process model. No empirical study, dataset or evaluation. Area descriptions still need to be fleshed out with domain experts, research questions and scenarios. Several of the agentic SE proposals it builds on were still under review at the time of writing.

evidence_notes.finding: Holding the agent pipeline fixed and varying only the communication architecture, a shared-state blackboard raises Coder-stage information fidelity by 62% and correct file targeting by 27.5 percentage points over message passing, yet end-to-end resolve rate improves only 4 points because all configurations converge to a ~22% conditional resolve rate once the right file is found. The bottleneck is the LLM's intrinsic diff-generation ability, not information quality or tool access, and the blackboard's gains cost 2.17x tokens and 1.61x latency.
evidence_notes.quote: Once the correct file is identified, however, all configurations converge to a ∼22% conditional resolve rate, revealing a downstream bottleneck in LLM diff generation.

extraction.framework: SE-Blackboard (pluggable Message-Passing, Blackboard and Hybrid communication modes over an identical agent pipeline, with a Pydantic state schema and role-bound write permissions)
extraction.benchmark: 50 SWE-bench Lite issues, evaluated with a new stage-level Information Fidelity Score (IFS) alongside resolve rate
extraction.baseline: message-passing multi-agent pipeline (with a Hybrid dual-channel condition as a third arm)
extraction.key_results: Blackboard improves Coder-stage IFS by 62% (0.586 vs 0.362, p=0.058) and correct file targeting by 27.5pp (82.6% vs 55.1%, Hybrid 78.1%). Conditional resolve rate once the correct file is targeted is statistically flat across modes (MP 22.2%, BB 21.1%, Hybrid 24.0%). End-to-end resolve rate is 16.0% vs 12.0% (a 33% relative gain), matching the information-flow bottleneck model's prediction that a 27.5pp targeting advantage yields roughly 6pp. Reviewer dynamics improve under BB (55 accept / 80 reject, first acceptance on iteration 1 in 21 runs, never accepted in 17) versus Hybrid (37/103, iteration-1 acceptance in 13, never in 29). A Toolformer-style tool-use ablation (read_file, search_code, read_lines, validate_patch, submit_patch) does not improve resolve rates for either mode and increases token consumption 2-4x; validate_patch detects format errors the LLM still cannot fix. BB costs 54,849 tokens/issue vs MP 25,316 (2.17x, Wilcoxon p<0.001) and 171s vs 106s latency (1.61x, p<0.001), with overhead concentrated in the Reviewer (28.2k vs 3.5k) that re-reads the serialized state each iteration; per resolved issue MP needs ~211k tokens, BB ~343k, Hybrid ~361k. Hybrid degrades via context overload, producing a 36% empty-patch rate where the Coder abandons patch emission entirely.
extraction.limitations: Internal validity: a single LLM (Claude Sonnet 4.5, temperature 0) removes model variance but limits generalizability, and the sequential pipeline introduces an ordering effect where a weak Planner analysis propagates downstream. External validity: 50 well-maintained Python SWE-bench Lite issues with Django overrepresented (22/50), and BB's resolve-rate advantage concentrates in easy Django issues, so the effect may partly reflect repository-specific factors; findings may not transfer to other languages or SE tasks beyond bug fixing. Construct validity: IFS uses rule-based entity extraction that can miss semantically equivalent references or count incidental mentions. Statistical validity: only 4 discordant pairs, McNemar underpowered, N≈300 needed for 80% power; the IFS result at p=0.058 does not reach significance; the tool ablation used only 10 issues per configuration and is treated as directional rather than a definitive null.

evidence_notes.finding: Wrapping an LLM in a generic AI agent (Suna) that can clone repositories, navigate sites, compile and orchestrate prompts produced usable end-to-end Selenium tests where direct chat-based prompting of the same models had failed to even compile. Model choice dominated outcome quality: Claude Sonnet 4 reached 70.1% successful tests versus DeepSeek V3's 34.3%, but the cheaper model was faster, never crashed, and produced largely disjoint error profiles, so the authors recommend a complementary incremental strategy.
evidence_notes.quote: In contrast, Claude Sonnet 4 exhibited a longer generation time but produced more consistent and higher-quality test cases.

extraction.framework: Suna (open-source generic AI agent) via OpenRouter, generating Selenium WebDriver + JUnit 5 tests
extraction.agent_count: 1 (single generic AI agent, configured with two different LLM backends)
extraction.benchmark: 9 real-world web applications (static, e-commerce, banking, UI-library and form-based), multiple generation sequences per site, scored from Maven Surefire reports
extraction.baseline: DeepSeek V3 0324 (free) vs Claude Sonnet 4 (paid) within the same agent; prior direct chat-based LLM prompting as an informal reference point
extraction.key_results: Claude Sonnet 4 produced 336 successful tests of 479 generated (70.1%); DeepSeek V3 produced 165 of 481 (34.3%). Error/failure rates were 23.4%/6.5% for Claude versus 49.1%/16.6% for DeepSeek, a 25.7pp error-rate and 10.2pp failure-rate reduction. Error profiles barely overlap: NoSuchElementException accounts for 50% of DeepSeek errors while TimeoutException accounts for 56.3% of Claude errors, intersecting only on ElementClickInterceptedException, NoSuchElementException and TimeoutException. Cost was $0.15 per successful test case for the paid model ($49.11 total). Per-site averages are much closer (33.8% vs 29%) because Claude produced no valid tests at all in several sequences whereas DeepSeek always produced compilable tests, which the authors read as evidence of stochastic, unpredictable agent behaviour even under controlled prompts.
extraction.limitations: Tests were generated black-box with no access to application source, and the study does not evaluate test quality or coverage, only compile-and-run success. No auto-fix or repair stage was implemented. The OpenRouter seed parameter was not used, so nondeterminism was uncontrolled. Only nine websites, one agent tool and two models were evaluated. The authors explicitly caution that hallucinations, nondeterminism, compliance and bias require human expert review of generated tests, especially in regulated domains.

evidence_notes.finding: In a multi-agent quantum debugging pipeline that separates detection (QBugFind) from repair (QBugFix) and validates with simulation-based total variation distance, iterative feedback dominates every other design choice: a single retry lifts Pass@1 from below 25% to above 80%. Elaborate prompting is not the lever — simple structured prompting beat Chain-of-Thought and ReAct for reasoning-capable models under fixed resource budgets.
evidence_notes.quote: Our results show that iterative feedback is critical, as a single retry raises Pass@1 from below 25% to above 80%.

extraction.framework: QBugLM (QBugGen mutation toolkit, QBugFind detection agent, QBugFix repair agent, QBugCheck deterministic validator) built on Strands Agents
extraction.agent_count: 2 LLM agents (finder and fixer) within a 4-component automated pipeline
extraction.benchmark: taxonomy-driven single-fault mutants injected into valid OpenQASM 3.0 programs from MQT Bench, scored with the unbiased Pass@k estimator over five independent runs per configuration and validated by simulation-based total variation distance
extraction.baseline: zero-retry single-shot debugging; Chain-of-Thought and ReAct prompting versus structured prompting; Claude 4.6 Sonnet versus Qwen3 Coder Next
extraction.key_results: A single retry raises Pass@1 from below 25% to above 80% for both models, with clearly diminishing returns afterwards; a two-retry budget is recommended as the accuracy/cost trade-off, after which Pass@5 reaches 100% in all categories. Each model retains exactly one unresolved weakness after two retries: Sonnet 4.6 reaches only 80% Pass@1 on structural errors while Qwen3 reaches only 92% on semantic deviation, which the authors read as model-specific rather than budget artifacts. Structured prompting achieves the highest Pass@1 for both models, outperforming CoT and ReAct. On structural errors, deprecated syntax and gate overuse, Qwen3 matches or beats Sonnet at 4.8x, 9.1x and 8.1x lower cost per mutant and 1.5-4.6x faster wall-clock time; semantic deviation is the sole exception, where Qwen3 burns ~350k tokens versus Sonnet's ~91k and still trails. The authors conclude deployment should be bug-type-aware rather than uniformly choosing the stronger model.
extraction.limitations: Class imbalance: six of the mutation strategies produce semantic deviations, so category-level results for C1-C3 are highly sensitive to single failures; mitigated by reporting per-category and aggregate results with five runs and an unbiased Pass@k estimator. Infrastructure failures such as network timeouts and per-agent context-window exhaustion are counted as unsuccessful fixes, which understates raw LLM capability but is deliberately conservative. Only single-fault injection, one mutant per operator, a limited circuit corpus and two models; compound bugs, regression detection, hybrid finder/fixer model pairings and comparison against static, dynamic and formal analyses are all left to future work.

evidence_notes.finding: The survey reports that multi-agent groups consistently outperform single agents on complex tasks needing diverse expertise (AgentVerse, DERA on MedQA, MetaGPT at 85.9%/87.7% Pass@1 on HumanEval/MBPP), while cataloguing the coordination failure modes that role-playing introduces: conversation deviation from the original objective, role flipping between assistant and user, and unreliable termination conditions. Structured intermediate artifacts and SOP-encoded workflows are identified as the main mitigation.
evidence_notes.quote: Role flipping happens when agents confuse their assigned roles, with the assistant providing instructions or the user attempting to execute tasks.

extraction.agent_count: surveyed frameworks range from 2-3 agents (CAMEL, DERA) to 5+ (MetaGPT, ChatDev) and 25 (Generative Agents)
extraction.benchmark: SWE-bench and SWE-bench Verified, HumanEval, MBPP, InterCode, WebArena, Mind2Web, OSWorld, AgentBench, HotPotQA
extraction.baseline: single-agent LLM baselines and ablated agent variants
extraction.key_results: Taxonomy of reasoning-enhanced, tool-augmented, multi-agent and memory-augmented agents over ~100 papers (2020-2024). MetaGPT's SOP-encoded workflow with mandatory structured intermediate artifacts (requirements documents, design artifacts, interface specifications) reaches 85.9%/87.7% Pass@1 on HumanEval/MBPP with a 100% task completion rate, explicitly reducing hallucination and inconsistency relative to less constrained multi-agent systems. ChatDev's chat chain uses 'communicative dehallucination' cross-checking as social verification. AgentVerse reports multi-agent groups consistently outperforming single agents with the largest gains on complex tasks; DERA's Researcher/Decider split significantly beats single-agent baselines on MedQA. SWE-bench progression: Claude 2 1.96%, Devin 13.86%, SWE-agent+GPT-4 12.47% (23.8% Verified), OpenHands+Claude 3.5 22.0% (41.0% Verified) — still far below human developers, with failures concentrated in deep code-context understanding, multi-file changes and complex debugging. Communication topologies are characterized as sequential handoff, hierarchical delegation and peer-to-peer collaboration; unstructured natural language gives flexibility but causes redundancy, ambiguity and information loss, while structured protocols improve efficiency at the cost of expressiveness. Cross-cutting limits are hallucination with real-world action consequences, long-horizon planning where error accumulation makes completion probability decay exponentially with step count, credit assignment, limited generalization under distribution shift, and prompt-injection/jailbreak security exposure.
extraction.limitations: Non-peer-reviewed preprint (Preprints.org) with an explicit publisher disclaimer. Narrative survey without a stated search protocol, inclusion criteria, screening process or quality appraisal, so selection bias is uncontrolled. Benchmark numbers are collated from the primary sources rather than independently reproduced, and coverage stops around late 2024 in a fast-moving field. No meta-analysis, and the claim that multi-agent groups outperform single agents is inherited from the surveyed papers rather than tested.

evidence_notes.finding: TEXT-FILE MISMATCH: the extracted text stored for this record is not the declared paper. The file contains 'Transparency in Frontier AI: What Leading Labs Are (and Aren't) Telling Us' by David Robusto — a transparency-scoring analysis of seven frontier AI models — with no BonsAIDE or IDE-interaction content anywhere in its 25 pages. It is not 'BonsAIDE: An Extended Vision for Human-AI Interaction in IDEs' (TOSEM, 10.1145/3793681). No extraction was performed, because attributing this content to the record's DOI would corrupt the evidence ledger. The artifact for this record needs to be re-retrieved before it can be read.
evidence_notes.quote: This study also exposes a stark divide in industry practices: established technology companies with diverse revenue streams maintain higher transparency, while new AI startups trend toward opacity.
